claim: The RACER-Knee randomized trial reported no meaningful 12-month patient benefit for Mako compared with conventional instruments and similar observed safety profiles.
source_or_reference: S3 | Parsons et al., Lancet 2026;408:924-934; doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(26)00986-4 | https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42624811/
notes: Search-indexed abstract reviewed. A correction dated 2026-10-24 is indexed (doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(26)02109-4); correction text was not retrieved. Use qualitative conclusion provisionally, not a numerical procurement threshold.

claim: The trial team reports comparable walking and early pain outcomes and higher resource use for robotic surgery in RACER-Knee.
source_or_reference: S4 | University of Warwick, trial-team release | https://warwick.ac.uk/news/pressreleases/robotic-assisted-knee/
notes: Full page read. Corroborates S3 but is the same trial, not independent replication; predates indexed correction. Manufacturer supported additional robotic procedure costs.

claim: A 68-patient single-centre ROSA randomized trial reported some early pain and flexion benefits, with no reported adverse events in its small sample.
source_or_reference: S5 | Neira et al., Knee 2026;61:104457; doi:10.1016/j.knee.2026.104457 | https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/42000386/
notes: Different platform and setting; cannot establish Mako benefit or rule out rare harm. Pain/flexion are not direct proof of earlier independent daily activities.
